issues.description: The problem statement (UML and textual specification) declares checkOrderReady() as a void method, but the Solution implementation defines public boolean checkOrderReady(). This is a signature mismatch: students implementing the method as void (per the spec) will produce a different method signature than the solution reference. Such a difference can cause confusion about the intended API (does checkOrderReady return a status or not?) and may mislead students who compare their implementation to the reference.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Solution's method signature match the problem specification. Change public boolean checkOrderReady() in SealSaloon.java to public void checkOrderReady(), and remove or internalize any returned boolean value (e.g., keep the internal servedAny variable for logic but do not return it). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to specify that checkOrderReady() returns a boolean and explain the meaning of the return value. Preferably keep the problem statement (void) and modify the solution to return void to avoid altering the intended public API.
